elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered §14.10: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate or to a successor organization ..." — the carve-out sits outside the consent requirement, so no IBM consent is needed for an Affiliate transfer.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same carve-out sentence now reads "a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets", capturing all three playbook triggers consent-free.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior written consent ..." — a direct restriction on the Vendor with no retained successor or affiliate exception.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...without Customer's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld ..." — the reasonableness standard is expressly attached to Customer's consent over IBM assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and will not assign to a competitor of Customer." This is an unconditional bar, not merely a consent-gated one, so it holds even if Customer were to consent.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "Customer's change of control gives IBM no right to terminate this Agreement." Express confirmation; the original contained no change-of-control trigger, so nothing retained contradicts it.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The new IBM sentence bars IBM assignment without Customer consent and contains no successor carve-out for IBM; only Customer has a consent-free successor right. (Immaterial here because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The Customer successor/Affiliate carve-out imposes no notice obligation, and no notice mechanic appears elsewhere in the rendered clause.
The retained Affiliate carve-out is a no-consent, non-successor exception, which under the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats a clean "other assignments require consent" result.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Both consent gates carry the qualifier: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld" for Customer-to-IBM and for IBM-to-Customer requests.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment. The fallback level is incomplete (no IBM successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and a retained no-consent Affiliate exception), but that is irrelevant once the preferred checklist is satisfied.

Minimal: the edit consists of two surgical changes — inserting "an Affiliate or" and "or sale of substantially all assets" into the existing carve-out, and adding one sentence covering Vendor assignment consent, the reasonableness standard, the competitor bar and the change-of-control confirmation. Nothing outside the checklist was added (no survival tail, no notice procedure, no re-pricing language) and no existing words were deleted.

Favourable retained language survives intact: the void-attempted-assignment sentence and Customer's continuing liability on permitted assignment are untouched, and the pre-existing "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard on IBM's consent to Customer assignments is preserved rather than replaced.
No dangling cross-references or contradictions: the original had no change-of-control provision, so the new confirmation sentence adds certainty without conflicting with any retained text.

One drafting check before sending: confirm "Affiliate" is a capitalised defined term in this Agreement. If it is not defined, use lowercase "an affiliate" with a short definition (e.g., an entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Customer) to avoid leaving an undefined term in §14.10.

Optional tightening, not required for completeness: consider adding "(including by way of assignment of this Agreement)" is unnecessary, but you may wish to state that the competitor bar applies notwithstanding any Customer consent — the current wording already reads as unconditional, so no change is needed unless IBM pushes back.
